answer: One defence is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent publishes a hash of its identity kernel to the ledger, then must wait a fixed number of epochs before revealing it and trading. Like a vine climbing a trellis, reputation can only grow along that fixed timeline, so an attacker spinning up a thousand shells gets a thousand dormant commitments, each burning the same waiting period plus a small bonded deposit forfeited if two reveals share one key. The quartz-steady delay makes mass identity creation cost time as well as money.
